title: Console minimalization strategy: rollforward criteria and scoped cuts for dashboards/tracing/costs
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: This ticket captures the scoped MVP cuts and the rollforward (graceful degradation) criteria for the Redwood Console observability surface focusing on three areas: dashboards (cards), trace sampling & thread-level tracing, and per-route cost breakdown. The goal is to produce a tightly-scoped launchable surface with clear acceptance criteria and a documented path to restore features after launch if capacity, cost, or telemetry constraints require it.
background: Multiple PM / Eng / Design reviews in Jan–Feb 2025 flagged telemetry ingestion costs and frontend complexity as blockers for the Console alpha. We need a defensible, testable minimal surface that provides value to internal customers (support/SEs) and early external adopters without incurring unacceptable SLO or cost risk. Existing related tickets: PM-41258, PM-24012, PM-11234 (see dependencies).
decision_record: We will ship a single-page Insight Stream (card-based) with 3 canonical cards: Route Success Rate (aggregated), 95p latency by model family (aggregated), and Token Cost per Route (daily rollup). Tracing will be limited to sampled end-to-end spans surfaceable via a lightweight link to a trace viewer; we will not ingest full span-level flamegraphs at 1:1 sampling. Per-request granularity and heavyweight trace queries are deferred to a Phase 2. Cost breakdowns will show daily and 7d rollups only; per-token interactive breakdowns are deferred. Rationale: unit-cost savings and reduced retention/ingestion while still enabling root-cause for common regressions.
tradeoffs: - User-visible tradeoff: fewer drilldowns and delayed granularity on cost; debugging rare tail-latency regressions will need a manual trace-on-demand flow.
acceptance_criteria: Insight Stream page reachable from Console nav with role-based access enforcement
Three cards rendered with 95th/median latency, success rate, and daily cost (last 14d) with <750ms median render time
Trace links open sampled traces in trace viewer UI, with sampling rate configurable per-environment, default 0.1%
Back-end query budget for the page capped and enforced (pre-aggregation TTL=24h) to keep infra cost within target budget
Metrics to validate: page load latency P50 <750ms, P95 <2s; observability ingestion delta < +12% for launch; user satisfaction survey score >=3.5/5 among alpha testers
QA: simulated noisy tenant test to confirm graceful failure modes when ingestion or DB is saturated (show cached last-good card with warning)
tasks: Finalize PRD and sign off with Eng/Design/SRE
Implement aggregated rollup pipelines for daily/7d metrics (pre-aggregation job + TTL)
Create lightweight trace-linking API (no full-span ingest) and config toggle for sampling
Design & implement three minimal cards in Console React shell
Instrumentation: add telemetry guardrails and budget checks in backend
E2E tests: perf/regression and saturation scenarios
Alpha rollout plan and stakeholder comms
notes: Design mockups: short-card widgets only, no interactive drilldowns. Engineering recommendation: pre-aggregate counts in job and store in small-timeseries table to avoid high-cardinality queries. SRE requested a hard query budget enforced by host-level throttling to avoid noisy tenant issues. If retention costs are still high after rollup, reduce retention window from 14d -> 7d as fallback.
